| Wales | Draw | Norway |
|---|---|---|
| **0.26** | **0.26** | **0.48** |

## 2. Confirmed facts
- **Results so far, confirmed:**
  - Portugal 1-0 Wales on 24 Sep in Lisbon. João Félix's long-range shot was deflected in off Ben Davies. Portugal "outshot Wales 19-4" ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/9/24/portugal-beat-wales-1-0-as-nations-league-defence-begins)).
  - Denmark 2-0 Wales on 27 Sep. The goals were a Ben Davies own goal and an Isaksen strike. Sky reports both came from Damsgaard deliveries ([Sky Sports](https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13591763/denmark-2-0-wales-craig-bellamys-side-bottom-of-nations-league-group-after-second-defeat-in-a-row), [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401861070)).

- **Standings:** Wales are bottom on 0 points with 0 goals. Norway are second on 3 points ([Sports Mole](https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/wales/uefa-nations-league/preview/wales-vs-norway-prediction-team-news-lineups_605956.html)).

- **Norway context:** this is their first League A campaign. beIN credits Haaland with 7 goals in 5 games at the 2026 World Cup.

## 3. Team news
**Wales (all from previews, not official squad releases)**
- **Reported out:** Harry Wilson, Joe Rodon (hamstring), Nathan Broadhead, Karl Darlow, Dylan Lawlor, Rubin Colwill, Isaak Davies. Football Faithful also lists David Brooks.
- **Impact:** losing Wilson and Rodon removes Wales' best chance-creator and their first-choice centre-back. That matters against Haaland.
- **Probable XI (Sports Mole and Football Faithful agree):** Ward; Roberts, Mepham, B. Davies, N. Williams; Ampadu, Sheehan; D. James, Johnson, Thomas; Koumas.
- **Disputed:** Koumas or Kieffer Moore up front. Sheehan or Jordan James next to Ampadu.

**Norway**
- **Confirmed out:** Alexander Sørloth (injury). David Møller Wolfe is available again after his suspension.
- **Ødegaard is uncertain.** He hurt his ankle in stoppage time against Portugal. Scans showed "no significant damage" ([Yahoo](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/martin-degaard-races-fit-wales-212438421.html), [Africa Soccer](https://africasoccer.com/odegaard-injury-doubt-for-norways-nations-league-meeting-with-wales/)). Solbakken said: "I wish I could say yes, but I don't know. I can't say no either."
- **Also doubts:** Thorstvedt and Ryerson.
- **Probable XI (Sports Mole):** Nyland; Aursnes, Ajer, Heggem, Ryerson; Ødegaard, Berge, Berg; Bobb, Haaland, Nusa.

**Unknown:** minutes limits for either side, the weather in Cardiff, the referee.

## 4. Tactics and matchups
- **Wales build-up and attack:**
  - Very little final-third output: 4 shots in Lisbon and no goals in two games.
  - Against Denmark, Bellamy switched to a "more traditional 4-4-2" with Moore as target man. Clwb Pêl-droed said "players appeared uncomfortable in their roles" ([Clwb Pêl-droed](https://clwbpeldroed.org/2026/09/28/wales-denmark-nations-league-points/)).
  - At home, Wales probably return to a 4-2-3-1 and rely on transitions through Johnson and Dan James.
- **Norway attack:**
  - A 4-3-3 that creates through Ødegaard, Bobb and Nusa for Haaland.
  - Haaland is clinical: 0.35 xG from 5 shots against Denmark, yet he scored twice.
- **Set pieces favour Norway:**
  - Wales conceded both Denmark goals from set pieces. Ampadu said that was frustrating because "We pride ourselves on being difficult to beat on set pieces."
  - Norway have height (Haaland, Ajer, Heggem) and Ødegaard's delivery.
  - But Norway also conceded a free-kick goal and a corner goal to Denmark.
- **Norway's defending is suspect:** five goals conceded in two games, which leaves Wales a counter-attacking route.
- **Expected goals:** I could not find verified xG totals for any of these matches, so I estimated from shot counts.
- **Rest and travel:** both teams played on 24 and 27 Sep, so rest is equal. Norway have a short flight. Wales have home advantage, and the Cardiff crowd is a real but modest boost.

## 5. How I got the numbers
- **Starting point:** Norway are the stronger side on talent and recent form, including the World Cup. A neutral-venue baseline is roughly Norway 52 / draw 25 / Wales 23.
- **Home advantage:** about +4 to +5 points for Wales.
- **Absences:** Wales' injuries move it back toward Norway.
- **Ødegaard doubt:** pulls it slightly toward Wales and the draw.
- **Comparison:** Sports Mole's model (32/25/43) is close but more generous to Wales. I am lower on Wales because they have no goals in two games and are missing Wilson and Rodon.

## 6. Counterarguments
- Wales have kept games tight: both defeats came from a deflection, an own goal or set pieces, not from being repeatedly opened up.
- Norway have conceded 5 goals in 2 games and are new to League A.
- If Ødegaard, Ryerson and Thorstvedt all miss out, Norway's control of midfield fades and a draw becomes much more likely.
- Wales have lost twice and must respond at home, which could lift their intensity.
- Norway might rotate after a long run of games since the World Cup.

## 7. Data issues
- Sky's article says the next game is "Thursday, September 30th". The match is on Thursday 1 October, so that is a date error and doesn't affect the analysis.
- ESPN's match report (gameId 401861073) blocked direct access with a 403. I only saw its title, via search results.

## 8. What would change the view during the game
- **Ødegaard confirmed out:** Norway down about 4 points, the draw up.
- **Haaland not starting:** Norway down about 8 points.
- **Wales start Moore in a 4-4-2 or a back five:** the draw goes up.
- **Live signals against the thesis:**
  - Norway's possession under 50% while Wales win transitions.
  - Wales ahead on shots after 30 minutes.
  - An early red card.
  - Heavy rain or wind that cuts down Norway's combination play.

- **Defending:** Norway are not watertight. They conceded two to Denmark and two to Portugal, so Wales scoring is realistic. The single most likely scoreline is around 1-1 or 1-2.

- **Pressure on Norway:** They are away from home with an injured captain and may carry fatigue after an intense first window.
- **A cautious Wales:** If Wales play the 5-4-1 that Goal predicts, a low-scoring game becomes more likely and the draw probability goes up.
